Subject: Environment scaling, license options & unit-econ — recap & next steps

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and concrete asks so we can move to a commercial proposal. High-level from our call:

- Use case: private VPC deployment for Helix clinical summarization and triage workflows (PHI in scope).
- Expected environments: PROD (3), STAGING (2), DEV (10) — please confirm below.
- Traffic profile (you mentioned): roughly 20–40M tokens / month initially; growth to ~80–120M/month in 12 months (ballpark).
- Key constraints: must be private (customer-managed VPC), FIPS/KMS integration, SOC2 evidence required.

Immediate asks for a tight price/quote: please confirm the following by EOD Monday so we can lock numbers into the project worksheet:
1) Confirm exact environment counts (prod/staging/dev / other).
2) Approx avg tokens per request and percent of requests that are short (<256 tokens) vs long (>1024 tokens).
3) Target unit economics: you mentioned wanting to keep below a target $/1M tokens — what is an acceptable range?
4) Procurement timeline and PO owner (procurement@? contact).

Preliminary pricing notes (so you have context before procurement):
- For private/VPC we typically offer either a) license + support per-environment with a committed token pool or b) committed token license (flat token-dollar commitment) with environment add-ons.
- Typical unit economics move materially with committed volume: small pilots (~<10M/mo) sit in $60–120 / 1M tokens; mid commits (50–150M/mo) typically land in $18–40 / 1M tokens depending on infra footprint & support band; very large commits (250M+/mo) can go below $15 / 1M tokens with density tuning and quantization.

I attached a short worksheet (pricing_cases_helix.xlsx) with three scenarios I will flesh out once I get your environment counts and target $/1M. Next step: once you confirm the items above, we will put together a formal SOW + pricing and loop in Security for KMS/SOC2 checklist.

Thanks,
--

Subject: Re: Environment scaling, license options & unit-econ — recap & next steps

Diego — thanks for the summary, that tracks. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed envs: PROD 3, STAGING 2, DEV 8 (we reduced dev from 10 -> 8). We also expect a small QA cluster (1) for nightly runs.
- Traffic: initial steady-state estimate is ~25M tokens / month (average today), we expect to peak to ~90M/month within 9–12 months as we onboard two more clinical sites. Typical request size is 300–800 tokens; ~60% short (<512), ~10% long (>1k).
- Budget: procurement has an initial target band of $150k–$275k annually for the first-year deployment including support. They asked if we can achieve approximately <$40 / 1M tokens as a pricing target; lower is better but procurement will be conservative.
- Procurement: procurement@helixhealth.com is the PO owner; Alex Morgan (alex.morgan@helixhealth.com) is the vendor ops lead. Target decision timeline: internal approvals by mid-April, PO by end of April.

Can you provide two concrete price scenarios that map to our target band: (A) conservative (no large commit, more env add-ons) and (B) committed token pool with 12-month commit? Also please include support tiers (Standard vs Premium) and what warranty/SLA differences look like for private/VPC installs.

Samantha
Samantha Green
Head of Integrations, Helix Health

Subject: Re: Environment scaling, license options & unit-econ — recap & next steps

Thanks Samantha — below are the two concrete scenarios you asked for (high level). I attached the pricing_cases_helix.xlsx with line-item math.

Scenario A — Conservative (env-based + minimal commit)
- License: per-environment seat/license fee: PROD $18k/env/yr, STAGING $6k/env/yr, DEV/QA $1.5k/node/yr
- Support: Standard (business hours, 24x5) included in license; Premium (24x7, on-call) +20% of license cost.
- Token usage: metered at $85 / 1M tokens (overage charge) for private installs with no token commit.
- Example math (your stated start = 25M/mo => 300M/yr): 300 * $85 = $25,500 per 1M? Sorry small correction: 300M tokens = 300 * 1M units; 300 * $85 = $25,500. That math is correct in terms of unit multiplier but unrealistic; to be clearer:
  - 300M tokens/year = 300 * 1M tokens units; at $85 / 1M => $85 * 300 = $25,500 (annual token charges) + env licenses (3*18k + 2*6k + 9*1.5k ~ $81k) => total ~$106.5k/yr (note: this conservative path tends to be pricier per-token but lowers upfront commitment).

Scenario B — Committed token pool + environment add-ons (recommended for 12-month private deployment)
- Commitment: 300M tokens/year committed -> blended $/1M = $32 / 1M tokens (example tier for 200–500M/yr).
- License: flat platform license $65k/yr (covers base infra + private control plane) + environment addons: PROD $8k/env, STAGING $3k/env, DEV/QA $750/node.
- Support: Premium available as a paid add-on (+15% of platform license for reg-level support & faster SLA).
- Example math (using your 300M/yr starting point): token cost = 300 * $32 = $9,600; license + env = $65k + (3*8k + 2*3k + 9*750 = $32,750) => total ~$107,350/yr. With Premium support (+15% of $65k ~ $9.75k) => ~$117k/yr.

Notes on unit-econ and your <$40 / 1M target:
- Scenario B hits your <$40 / 1M target handily at $32 / 1M for a 300M/yr commit. If you land at ~90M/mo (1,080M/yr), we can push below $15 / 1M with additional infra density/quantization work and longer-term commits.
- The per-environment license model (Scenario A) skews toward larger license line items and higher per-token overage. Committed pools (Scenario B) provide predictability and materially better unit economics once you cross the 150–200M/yr threshold.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm final env counts and we finalize the 2 scenarios in the spreadsheet.
- If Scenario B looks reasonable, I will draft a statement-of-work + T&Cs and loop Security/Privacy to start the KMS and SOC2 evidence exchange.
- Marissa / Karthik: once Samantha confirms, can you prepare a draft commercial (worksheet-driven) and an SOW stub? I already attached the starter SOW (redwood-deploy-sow-draft.pdf).

Diego
